:::{#sol-direct-sum-equiv-practice}

Both $(1, 0, 0)$ and $(0, 1, 0)$ lie in $\mathcal{S}_1$,
and they are [linearly independent](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-linearly-independent),
so they are a [basis](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-basis) of $\mathcal{S}_1$
and $\dim(\mathcal{S}_1) = 2$.
The single nonzero vector $(0, 1, 1)$ is a basis of $\mathcal{S}_2$,
so $\dim(\mathcal{S}_2) = 1$.
Then

$$
\dim(\mathcal{S}_1) + \dim(\mathcal{S}_2) = 2 + 1 = 3 = \dim(\reals^3),
$$

so by statement 2 of @thm-direct-sum-equiv, $\reals^3 = \mathcal{S}_1 \oplus \mathcal{S}_2$.

:::
